item.title: US charges three men for allegedly plotting attack on UK base
item.description:
The U.S. charged three individuals in connection with alleged Iranian-linked terror plots, including a September scheme against a British Royal Air Force Base that housed U.S. military personnel and aircraft, per an indictment unsealed Tuesday. The big picture: The indictment alleges that a leader of an Islamic terrorist group attempted to coordinate with his fellow defendants from jail by passing coded messages through third parties. Driving the news: Since early in the year, the three men named in the indictment worked to commit terror attacks on behalf of an Iran-aligned terrorist network, the indictment alleges. This is a breaking news story and will be updated.

item.title: Kennedys sue to block Trump's arch, arguing it would cast shadow on JFK's grave
item.description:
250ft arch risks ‘permanently diminishing’ memorials to ex-president and relatives at Arlington cemetery, lawsuit says Nine members of the Kennedy family political dynasty have sued the Trump administration , asking a federal judge to block the president’s plan to build a towering, gilded arch they say would cast a shadow over their relatives’ graves in Arlington national cemetery. The family’s complaint states that the 25oft triumphal arch, topped with a Lady Liberty-like winged figure, would “obstruct the clear sightline of the Kennedy Gravesites” and “fundamentally alter the experience of visiting” their family’s memorial at Arlington national cemetery. The project, they argued in a statement, risks “permanently diminishing these memorials”. Continue reading...

item.title: In Mississippi, voters await cliffhanger Senate result with hope and frustration
item.description:
Mississippi, a state not known for close elections, now sits in the center of the national spotlight as an unusually high number of absentee and provisional ballots will determine the size of the Democratic majority in the Senate. In partnership with the Pulitzer Center, Liz Landers reports on how election officials are handling the ongoing vote count and the historic nature of this Senate race.

item.title: Federal judge allows Trump’s $10bn defamation lawsuit against BBC to proceed
item.description:
From today's decision by Judge Jeffrey Kuntz (S.D. Fla.) in Trump v. BBC : In Trump v. CNN (S.D. Fla. 2023), aff'd (11th Cir. 2025), Judge Singhal concluded that "the complained of statements are opinion, not factually false statements, and therefore are not actionable." In Trump v. Dow Jones & Co., Inc. (S.D. Fla. 2026), Judge Gayles dismissed President Trump's claims that the Wall Street Journal failed to adequately investigate claims it reported. Those cases involved a news entity reporting on a story. Here, the news entity created the story. BBC admitted as much by confirming it had edited a video to make it appear as though President Trump made a statement he never made. And it acknowledged it chose to release the video in a documentary only a week before the 2024 Presidential Election, at the time it would have the most impact. Several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released, according to the Paris public prosecutor’s office. item.title: After midterm rout, Republicans can still confirm a Supreme Court justice, but at what cost?
item.description:
The Supreme Court is seen through a car window reflecting the U.S. Capitol dome on Nov. 9, 2026. AP Photo/Allison Robbert The 2026 midterm rout that awarded Democrats decisive majorities in the Senate and House has also sparked interest in the future of the U.S. Supreme Court . With Democrats securing at least a 54-seat majority in the Senate on Jan. 3, 2027 , the window is rapidly closing for President Donald Trump to appoint a new Supreme Court justice and safeguard conservative dominance on the court for decades. As a Supreme Court scholar , I know that judicial appointments have real consequences. Look no further than Roe v. Wade : Within two years of securing a 6–3 conservative majority, the high court in 2022 eliminated the constitutional right to abortion that had existed for almost 50 years. Now that Democrats have taken the Senate, if a Republican-appointed justice retires…
